name: Dilmun Burial Mounds
description: On the western side of Bahrain's main island, thousands of small stone-and-earth burial mounds stretch across the landscape, built between 2200 and 1750 BCE. About 11,774 survive, along with 17 royal tombs that once rose as two-storey towers. They were the resting places of a trading people, the Early Dilmun civilization, whose wealth let ordinary islanders be buried with ceremony too.
